claims.text: Frequent Facebook interaction is directly associated with greater psychological distress.
Frequent Facebook interaction is indirectly associated with greater psychological distress via a two-step pathway that increases communication overload and reduces self-esteem.
Communication overload mediates the psychological distress and mental health implications of social media interaction.

evidence.description: Structural equation modeling on a survey of 513 college students demonstrated a direct relationship between frequent Facebook interaction and higher psychological distress.
Structural equation modeling confirmed a two-step mediation pathway where frequent Facebook interaction raises communication overload, which in turn lowers self-esteem and leads to distress.
Structural equation model analysis assessed communication overload as an underlying mechanism linking Facebook interaction to mental health outcomes in N=513 college students.

methodologies.name: Structural Equation Modeling
methodologies.description: Used structural equation modeling on survey data from college students to assess direct and mediating pathways between social media interaction and psychological distress.
